title: Client-side context resolver heuristics (scratchpad)
content:
Notes to self - client-side context resolver heuristics (working draft)

Goal:
- Provide a compact library inside the client SDK that picks, merges, and trims context slices before hitting the API. Reduce tokens sent, preserve salience, and avoid repeated server-side merges.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Clients may have partial local state (recent conversation, local KV, ephemeral user edits).
- Bandwidth / latency matter: prefer local decisions that avoid extra round-trips.
- Server still authoritative for identity/long-term memory but client can heuristically surface most-relevant slices.

Design ideas (high level):
1) ContextSlice: {id, source, timestamp, priority_score, tokens_estimate, compacted_text}
   - source: one of [recent-msg, local-notes, assistant-summary, user-kv, embeddings-cache]

2) Resolver API (client SDK):
- resolveContext(slices[], budget_tokens, mode) -> ordered list of slices to attach
  - mode: fast|balanced|precise
  - budget_tokens: maximum token-length to send (including system + input)

Example payload shape (client -> local resolver call):
{
  "slices": [
    {"id":"r1","source":"recent-msg","timestamp":"2026-02-20T12:01:23Z","priority_score":0.9,"tokens_estimate":120},
    {"id":"kb42","source":"user-kv","timestamp":"2025-08-01T08:00:00Z","priority_score":0.2,"tokens_estimate":40}
  ],
  "budget_tokens": 800,
  "mode": "balanced"
}

Heuristic ranking (sketch):
- base_score = recency_weight * f(recency) + source_boost + semantic_relevance + manual_pin
- adjust: if slice.tokens_estimate > large_threshold -> consider compacting (head/tail + summary)

Compaction strategies (local):
- head-tail: keep first N and last M lines when slice looks like multi-turn transcript
- sentence-extract: choose top-k sentences by BM25 against prompt tokens (cheap)
- abstractive-local-summary: call small on-device LM (optional) to compress a long slice into ~50 tokens

Pseudocode resolver:

function resolveContext(slices, budget, mode):
  normalized = normalizeScores(slices)
  sorted = sortBy(normalized, desc)
  selected = []
  tokens_used = 0
  for s in sorted:
    if tokens_used + s.tokens_estimate <= budget:
      selected.push(s)
      tokens_used += s.tokens_estimate
    else:
      // try compacting
      compacted = compactIfWorthIt(s, remaining=budget - tokens_used)
      if compacted and tokens_used + compacted.tokens <= budget:
        selected.push(compacted)
        tokens_used += compacted.tokens
      // else skip
  return selected

CompactIfWorthIt heuristics:
- estimate quality_loss = qualityModelPredict(s, compacted_form) (cheap classifier)
- allow compaction if quality_loss < threshold(mode) and token_gain > X

Interaction diagram (ASCII):
Client App -> Client Resolver (local lib) -> Selected Slices -> Redwood API
                              |
                              v
                       Optional local small LM (for abstractive summarization)

Edge cases / unresolved:
- Conflicting slices (different versions of same entity): prefer pinned user edits, then recency, then server-authority tag. Need TTL for stale local copies.
- Privacy: some slices are sensitive (PII). Clients should mark slices with sensitivity tag; resolver must not send sensitive slices unless explicitly allowed by user.
- Determinism: want deterministic selection under same inputs for caching and reproducibility. Seeds may be derived from session id.

Testing ideas:
- Fuzzer that generates random slice sets and checks preservation of annotated "gold" spans under multiple budgets.
- Offline eval: measure token reduction vs recall of reference answers (precision@k of spans included).

Telemetry to collect (lowest-privacy footprint):
- resolver_version, mode, budget_requested, tokens_sent, number_of_slices, compaction_used(true/false), hit_rate_against_server_recall

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we coordinate with server-side prefix caching? E.g., avoid client packing information the server already has cached. Need a small cache-key handshake or TTL header.
- Best default mode for new apps? propose "balanced" with budget = min(1024, remaining_request_budget)
- UX surface for "pinning" slices in the client (api for end-developers).
- Small LLM cost vs token savings tradeoff for abstractive-local-summary: run experiments with quantized 125M model.

Notes to Marco: please sanity-check compaction thresholds and add typical tokens_estimate heuristics based on utf8 word counts.

-- end --
